endorsements.title: CHAI AI governance frameworks (playbooks)
endorsements.quote: Vendor should provide recurring disaster recovery summaries.

endorsements.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework: Generative AI Profile (NIST AI 600-1)
endorsements.issuer: National Institute of Standards and Technology
endorsements.quote: Additionally, establish warning systems to determine if a GAI system is being used in a new domain where previous assumptions (relating to context of use or mapped risks such as security, and safety) may no longer hold.

endorsements.title: CHAI Responsible AI Guide (Assurance Standards Guide)
endorsements.quote: The risk management plan should be accompanied by the design of a patient safety focused process and a framework for the measurement, analysis and improvement of processes and the AI solution, including document control and records, configuration management and control, access controls, change management and managing outsourced processes.

endorsements.title: Developing, purchasing, implementing and monitoring AI tools in radiology: practical considerations. A multi-society statement
endorsements.issuer: ACR, CAR, ESR, RANZCR, RSNA; Radiol Artif Intell 2024 (PMID 38251899, doi:10.1148/ryai.230513)
endorsements.quote: How will the AI tool be integrated into the institutions’ workflows and how can the commercial claims be verified and monitored?

endorsements.title: Adoption of AI in Healthcare Delivery Systems: Early Applications and Impacts
endorsements.quote: When an organization shares whether ambient scribe is or is not “working” for them, it is crucial to understand the specific goals they were hoping to achieve from the outset.

commentary.bottom_line: Five frameworks and guidance documents endorse recurring review of deployed AI vendors, but no supplied study tests whether such reviews detect declining performance or improve renewal decisions. The recommendation currently rests on expert consensus rather than measured outcomes.

perspectives.view: No supplied study tests recurring vendor review, and no supplied study documents the hazard of unreviewed vendor decline. Certainty cannot be rated above no direct evidence. The five endorsements come from frameworks and multi-society guidance, which reflect expert agreement but do not show effect on performance, safety, or value.

The NIST Generative AI Profile calls for warning systems when a system moves into a new domain, and the CHAI Assurance Standards Guide calls for document control and change management. These are voluntary framework expectations. The sources supplied do not tie vendor review cadence to any binding federal or state requirement.

The ambient scribe guidance advises that organizations define their goals at the outset, which suggests a renewal review needs a baseline to compare against. The radiology statement asks how commercial claims will be verified and monitored. Neither source reports the staff time or cost of running recurring reviews.

commentary.research_gap: No study compares organizations that conduct scheduled vendor performance reviews with those that do not, measuring detection of performance drift, safety events, contract changes, or renewal outcomes. Studies are also needed on what review interval and which metrics give useful signal at acceptable staff burden.
commentary.underserved_note: No study tested the practice, so no evidence covers Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy populations. Safety-net systems may have less contracting and analytic staff to run reviews, and vendor performance in these populations may go unmeasured unless reviews stratify results by patient group.
